name: The Courant

text: The press itself, through a glass wall, running.
Forty thousand copies before dawn, and the whole building shakes with it.
A card says the noise is the reason nobody here can whisper.
The morning's front page, still wet, pinned up as it comes off.
NORTHERN LINE STILL SHUT. RENTS AGAIN. A DOG, APPARENTLY.
Column four is a full page from the Foundation about storm safety, unpaid.
The spike: everything the editor threw out this week, on a nail.
Most of it is nothing. Three of them are about boats.
They are the same story from three different harbours, and it did not run.
Bound volumes of the Courant, one per year, going back to 1004.
Anybody may read them. There is a stool and a lamp and no questions asked.
The volume for 1052 is out on the desk, and nobody will say who asked for it.
The public counter. Notices, births, deaths, and lost Kin, a penny a line.
The lost-Kin column is the longest in the paper and always has been.
It is also the only column the Courant has never charged for.
The masthead, in a frame, with the founding sentence under it:
A CITY THIS SIZE CANNOT SEE ITSELF WITHOUT HELP.
It is a good sentence too. This city is full of good sentences.
The morgue: clippings, filed by subject, going back four decades.
The drawer marked MERIDIAN FOUNDATION is the fullest in the room
and almost every cutting in it is somebody being thanked.
The drawer marked LOST AT SEA is thinner and better ordered.
One folder in it has been taken out and put back so many times
the tab has worn through and been rewritten twice.
A desk with three months of the same investigation on it,
held together with string, and a note to the editor on top
reading: I KNOW. I KNOW. GIVE ME ONE MORE WEEK.
A map of the city on the wall stuck with pins where reporters are.
Twenty-two districts, eleven pins.
A city of this size is mostly unwatched, and everyone in this room knows it.

_plan: The newspaper is the room where the player can see the truth being nearly found by people who are not them. Three harbour stories that are the same story, spiked. A LOST AT SEA folder handled until the tab wore through. A reporter three months in asking for one more week. Nothing is confirmed, nobody names anybody, and the Foundation drawer is genuinely full of thank-yous.
